key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings achieve better long-term corrosion and wear performance when droplet flattening is high and coating porosity is low, while higher humidity further reduces friction and wear through tribo-chemical effects.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters to produce dense, fine-lamellar amorphous coatings can improve durability of steel surfaces exposed to corrosive and variable-humidity service environments.
method: Fe-based amorphous coatings were detonation-sprayed onto Q235 carbon steel under different spraying parameters.
Coating microstructure was examined through droplet morphology, circularity, expansion factor, and porosity.
Corrosion and tribology performance were evaluated across different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and wear testing, showing that coatings with more porosity had poorer long-term corrosion resistance, while friction coefficient and wear rate decreased as humidity increased.
watch_item: Performance is sensitive to spraying-induced porosity and environmental humidity, so process control and service-condition matching are critical for reliable deployment.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
